sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for respondent Nos.1 & 2.
Respondent No.3 though served in this matter, has remained unrepresented before this Court.

3. F.I.R. in Crime No.45/2024 was initially registered by Keragodu Police Station, Mandya, against the petitioner herein for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 21.03.2024 received from respondent No.2 who is the Child Department Project Officer of Keragodu Circle,
Mandya District.
4. During the course of investigation of the case petitioner herein was arrested on 25.03.2024 and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed against two persons.
Petitioner is arrayed as accused No.2 in the charge sheet.
Bail application filed by the petitioner before the Trial Court in Spl.C.No.150/2024 was rejected on 02.09.2024.

Therefore, he is before this Court.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner is a youngster aged about 21 years having no criminal antecedents.
Victim girl has not made any allegation against the petitioner in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C before the Jurisdictional Magistrate.
The DNA test report does not support the allegation made against the petitioner.
Accordingly, he prays to allow this petition.
6. Per contra, learned HCGP who has opposed the petition, however, does not dispute the submission made by the learned Counsel for the petitioner.

7. FIR in the present case was initially registered against the petitioner on the basis of the first information received from respondent No.2 who had approached the police on the basis of the information given by the victim girl who was pregnant by seven months.
8. During the course of the investigation petitioner herein was arrested on 25.03.2024 and remanded to NC: 2024:KHC:45146 judicial custody.
After completion of the investigation charge sheet has been filed against two persons.
The statement of the victim girl under Section 164 of Cr.PC was recorded by the Jurisdictional Magistrate on 30.03.2024.
The victim girl has stated that she was in love with accused No.1/Yogesh and she had met him 6-7 times.
When she had gone to the hospital for her medical examination, she was informed that she was pregnant.
She had informed the same to Yogesh, who had told her that he would get some tablets to her.
Subsequently, marriage of Yogesh was performed with another girl.
Thereafter she started loving the petitioner herein and he had met her once.
She has not made any allegation against the petitioner about committing any sexual assault on her.
DNA test report which is received in this case reflects that victim girl is the biological mother of the male baby born to her and accused No.1/Yogesh is the biological father of the said male baby.
Petitioner herein is excluded from being the biological father of the male baby born to the victim girl.
Petitioner aged about 21 years who NC: 2024:KHC:45146 has no other criminal antecedents is in custody from 25.03.2024.

Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter,
I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively.
Accordingly, the following:-
ORDER The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is directed to be enlarged on bail in SPL.C.No.150/2024 pending before the Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge FTSC-II Mandya, arising out of Crime No.45/2024 registered by Keragodu Police Station, Mandya District for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(i)(N), 354(D), 376(3) & 450 of IPC and Sections 4, 5(j), 6 & 12 of the of Protection of Children from sexual Offences Act,
2012, subject to the following conditions:
